title: Kansas's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Kansas's 2nd Congressional District will be held on November 3, 2026, with primaries on August 4, 2026. The district covers eastern Kansas from Nebraska to Oklahoma, including Topeka, Emporia, Junction City, and Pittsburg, as well as portions of Kansas City and Lawrence. Incumbent Republican Derek Schmidt, first elected in 2024, is seeking a second term after succeeding retiring Rep. Jake LaTurner. He faces a Republican primary challenge from Chad Young, while Democrats Don Coover and Braeden Curwick (though Curwick may have withdrawn) vie for their party's nomination, and Libertarian John Hauer is running in the general election. The race is rated 'Solid R' by major nonpartisan forecasters, reflecting the district's strong Republican lean.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026. The race is rated 'Solid R' by The Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball.

candidates.name: Derek Schmidt
candidates.summary: Derek Schmidt is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Kansas's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. He previously served as Kansas Attorney General from 2011 to 2023 and in the Kansas State Senate from 2001 to 2011. Schmidt is a fifth-generation Kansan who focuses his campaign on supporting Republican majorities in Congress, border security, lowering costs, and advancing policies aligned with the Trump administration.

candidates.name: Chad Young
candidates.summary: Chad Young is a Republican candidate running for the U.S. House in Kansas's 2nd Congressional District. A Lawrence resident and founder of the Life Skills Programs, a nonprofit for troubled youths, Young previously ran for this seat in 2024. His campaign platform focuses on abolishing federal agencies including the IRS, FBI, and CIA, eliminating taxes, and reducing the size of the federal government.

candidates.name: Don Coover
candidates.summary: Don Coover is a Democratic candidate for the U.S. House in Kansas's 2nd Congressional District. A West Point graduate, U.S. Army veteran (military intelligence pilot), and veterinarian who earned his degree from Kansas State University, Coover runs a cattle genetics company and veterinary practice on his ranch in Galesburg, Kansas. His campaign focuses on addressing the rising cost of living, opposing tariffs that harm agriculture, protecting rural hospitals, and reducing the national debt.

candidates.name: John Hauer
candidates.summary: John Hauer is the Libertarian Party candidate for the U.S. House in Kansas's 2nd Congressional District. He previously ran as the Libertarian nominee for the same seat in the 2024 general election, receiving approximately 3% of the vote. The Libertarian Party nominates by convention rather than primary, and Hauer is listed on Ballotpedia as running in the 2026 general election.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race (zero polls as of June 2026), so confidence is reduced to medium and the forecast relies entirely on structural race indicators. Those indicators are consistently and strongly favorable to Republicans: the district is described as having a strong Republican lean, and all three major nonpartisan forecasters (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) rate it 'Solid R'. Incumbent Republican Derek Schmidt, a former Kansas Attorney General, is seeking a second term after winning the open seat in 2024. His primary challenger Chad Young holds fringe policy positions (abolishing the IRS, FBI, CIA), making it unlikely he defeats the incumbent in the primary. Democratic candidate Don Coover has a credible background (West Point graduate, Army veteran, veterinarian/rancher) but faces long odds in a district that strongly favors Republicans. Libertarian John Hauer received approximately 3% in 2024. With no polling to measure exact dynamics, the structural indicators overwhelmingly support a safe Republican hold.
